brief.situation: You are the identity and AVD administrator at Merrow Insurance. Yesterday afternoon a colleague created the Conditional Access policy CA-AVD-MFA, requiring MFA for Azure Virtual Desktop, and selected every app whose name contained 'Azure Virtual Desktop'. This morning users who refresh Windows App get an empty or failing workspace feed. 100 new hires start onboarding on AVD at 09:00.
handover: Security requires MFA for all AVD connections; that is not negotiable.
Single sign-on is enabled on the host pools.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the Conditional Access policy, the three AVD-related apps it can target and the feed users load.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the record: why feeds failed after the MFA policy, what you changed, and how MFA stayed in force.

parts.label: Why
parts.modelAnswer: Sign-in failures were all on the Azure Virtual Desktop Azure Resource Manager Provider, under CA-AVD-MFA. The policy included that app, which only retrieves the feed and should not have MFA.

parts.label: Change
parts.modelAnswer: CA-AVD-MFA now targets only Azure Virtual Desktop and Windows Cloud Login; a pilot's feed loaded and the connection required MFA.

parts.label: MFA kept
parts.criteria: Does not trade security for the deadline.
parts.modelAnswer: Disabling the policy would have removed MFA for all AVD connections on 100 new hires' first day. The targets are documented and changes need a What If on a pilot first.

expertPath.text: Failures all on the ARM Provider app; policy includes 50e95039; all users affected; What If shows new hires will fail.

noMfa.headline: Fix the target, keep the control
noMfa.body: The policy was right in what it required and wrong in one target. Remove the feed app from it; MFA stays on the apps that need it.

onboardingStalled.body: The Azure Resource Manager Provider app only retrieves the feed and should not have MFA. Target Azure Virtual Desktop and Windows Cloud Login only.

scoring.modelReasoning: Sign-in failures are all on the feed app, the Azure Virtual Desktop Azure Resource Manager Provider, which the new policy includes. Microsoft's guidance is to target Azure Virtual Desktop and Windows Cloud Login and never the provider app. Remove that one target, keep MFA on the others, and check with a pilot. Disabling the policy removes MFA for everyone; MFA re-registration changes nothing. Document the targets and require a What If for changes.
